name: table
source: src/components/crud/_base-grid.vue (MGrid) — wraps the Kendo Vue Grid (@progress/kendo-vue-grid) + gridWorker/arrayWorker. Usually driven by FlotoPaginatedCrud.
summary: The product's primary data table. Resizable/reorderable/sortable columns, client + server paging, grouping, selection (with bulk-action bar), expandable detail rows, per-column cell slots. MGrid is the grid; FlotoPaginatedCrud is the fetch+paginate wrapper around it.

variants.name: pivot
variants.what: pivot/report grid (grouping, group-collapsible=false: no chevron, all rows always visible)

variants.name: editable
variants.what: [element] inline editing — a pencil per row; columns with editable:true become obs-inputs while editing, with Save/Cancel (obs-link)

variants.name: footer-split
variants.what: pagination footer DEFAULT — pager (first/prev/pages/next/last + page-size) on the LEFT, item total ('1 - 50 of 222 items') on the RIGHT. Used when the `footer` slot is empty.

variants.name: footer-centered
variants.what: pagination footer with a CENTERED band — pager LEFT, slotted `footer` content (e.g. a severity legend) CENTERED, item total RIGHT. Auto-selected by filling the `footer` slot (the product Monitors list page).

variants.name: style-variants
variants.what: [element] variant: bordered (internal grid, no outer frame) | borderless-rows (no row dividers, airy) · header-style: default | tinted · hide-header (compact widget grids)

states.name: hover
states.what: row highlight; the primary (first / primary:true) record-name cell gets a DOTTED UNDERLINE (its clickable-name affordance)

states.name: header-rules
states.what: [element] the header row carries a rule ABOVE and BELOW it (border-top + border-bottom via --border-color), matching the product

states.name: editing
states.what: [element] a row in inline-edit mode — editable cells are obs-inputs, Save/Cancel shown

columns.note: column defs. obs-table: [{key,title,width?,align?,sortable?,type?,editable?,colorKey?,primary?}] — a column with primary:true is the PRIMARY (record-name) column: heavier weight (500) + a dotted underline on ROW hover; if NO column sets it, the FIRST data column is primary automatically (works for a text OR a severity first column). — type: text (default) | severity (composes <obs-severity> dot + the row's name; level from the row's sev/severity field) | dot (composes <obs-severity> dot + its level label) | status (obs-tag) | type (server/cog icons) | tags (obs-tag chips) | sparkline (inline trend line) | heat (cell filled with the --severity token named by the row's colorKey field) | bar (inline relative-percent bar) | logo (COLOURED brand/vendor mark(s) via obs-logo — cell value = a logo name string, an object {name,variant?,size?,title?}, or an ARRAY of those rendered side by side; variant defaults to 'color', use variant:'line' for a monochrome secondary mark) | icon (a single clickable obs-icon that emits `cellaction`, OR an ARRAY value → each name rendered as a glyph side by side). editable:true marks the column editable when the table has `editable`. product MGrid: {field,title,width,cell,sortable}

rows.note: [element] obs-table rows [{id, …}] (the product MGrid names this `data`)

selected.note: [element] obs-table selected id array; reflects to el.selected

sortable.note: [element] obs-table: enable sorting on columns with sortable:true

page-size.note: [element] obs-table: 0 → no pagination; >0 → paginate (product MGrid uses default-page-size/paging)

group-by.note: [element] obs-table: group rows under collapsible group-header rows (with counts) by a column key

group-collapsible.note: [element] obs-table: when combined with group-by. true (default) = collapsible bands (chevron + count, click to collapse). false = pivot/report grid: no chevron, no count, every child row is always visible (a static report layout)

editable.note: [element] obs-table: inline editing. Adds a pencil column per row; while a row is edited, each column marked `editable:true` becomes an obs-input. Emits `edit` (id) on entering edit, `save` ({id, values}) on Save, `canceledit` on Cancel

variant.note: [element] obs-table: default | bordered (internal column+row grid, NO outer left/right frame) | borderless-rows (no row dividers, just the header underline, airy spacing)

hide-header.note: [element] obs-table: hide the header row (compact widget grids)

selectable.note: checkbox column + selection. [element] obs-table: a FIRST-CLASS optional toggle — when set, a select-all header checkbox + a per-row checkbox column appear (indeterminate on partial selection, reflects el.selected); when unset, there is NO checkbox column and the leading data cell keeps the same tight left inset. Checkboxes are optional by design; no extra prop needed.

full-width.note: [element] obs-table: width behaviour (two modes). false (default) = a slight left/right INSET (the leading cell keeps its left pad, the trailing cell its right pad). true = FLUSH edge-to-edge — those side pads are removed so cell content, the header rule, the per-row dividers and the hover background all run to the table's left/right edges with no side gutter. Attribute: full-width.

searchTerm.note: external search; with use-search-term-loading shows a spinner

tree.note: [element] obs-table: hierarchical rows — each row has a `children` array; chevron + indent per level (starts expanded)

slots.perColumn: a slot per column field renders that cell (status, name, tags, severity, value, duration, action, monitorType, timestamp, count, …)
slots.footer: content CENTERED in the pagination footer between the pager (left) and the item total (right) — e.g. a severity legend. Filling it switches the footer from the SPLIT variant to the CENTERED variant; leave empty for split.
slots.bulk-actions: the action buttons for the floating BULK ACTION BAR (obs-toolbar variant=bulk). When rows are selected, obs-table shows a centered, floating bar just above the pager with the selection count + a clear, and projects these buttons into it (e.g. Acknowledge / Assign / Delete). Put slot="bulk-actions" on each REAL element (not a <template>).

events.edit: [element] obs-table (editable): a row entered inline-edit mode — payload is the row id
events.save: [element] obs-table (editable): inline edit saved — payload {id, values} with the edited draft
events.canceledit: [element] obs-table (editable): inline edit cancelled — draft discarded

decisionFlow: Just a few static key/values for ONE record, not a dataset? -> obs-key-value (a definition/detail list), NOT a grid.
A short list of big metric/KPI values (value + unit + label), not rows-of-records? -> obs-metric-list, NOT a grid.
Need to fetch + paginate a list with CRUD? -> FlotoPaginatedCrud (wraps MGrid; handles fetch/paging/search/filters). [element] obs-table with columns + rows.
Have data already in memory to show in a table? -> MGrid with :data + :columns. [element] obs-table columns + rows.
Large/server dataset? -> MGrid server paging (external-take/external-skip + total-count + @data-state-change).

Rows edited in place (no separate form/drawer)? -> [element] obs-table `editable` (a pencil per row; columns with editable:true become obs-inputs, Save/Cancel). For a full record form use a drawer/modal instead.
Rows need actions? -> a row-actions kebab cell (FlotoGridActions); multi-select -> selectable + the bulk-action bar.
Rows have drill-down detail? -> expandable + the detailRow slot.
Genuinely hierarchical (parent/child levels)? -> [element] obs-table `tree` (rows carry a `children` array; chevron + indent per level).

Rows bucketed under group headers with counts? -> `grouping` ([element] group-by). If it's a static report where children never collapse (no chevron, all rows always visible) -> add group-collapsible="false" (the pivot/report grid).
Columns need rich rendering (status tag, severity dot/ring, tags, sparkline, heat cell, percent bar, type icons)? -> per-column `type` on the column (cell-types).

crudList.useWhen: a fetched, paginated, searchable list (the default)

expandable.example: discovered services, trace spans, interface details

basic.useWhen: You have a plain dataset to render as columns + rows with sortable headers — either data already in memory (`MGrid` with `:data` + `:columns`) or a fetched/paginated/searchable list page (the default, via `FlotoPaginatedCrud`, which wraps MGrid and owns fetch/paging/search/filters). The main `.k-grid` data-grid header (transparent, UPPERCASE, 600) is the standard chrome.
basic.dontUse: Don't use a grid for a handful of static key/values — use a definition list / cards instead. If rows need multi-select bulk operations use `selectable`; if each row has drill-down detail use `expandable`; if rows must be grouped with counts use `grouping`; if the dataset is large/server-driven use `pagination` with server paging.
basic.example: Settings list views and inventory monitor lists rendered via FlotoPaginatedCrud; drill-down sub-tables and preview grids rendered via MGrid :data :columns.

grouping.useWhen: Rows should be bucketed under group headers with per-group counts, and each band can COLLAPSE. In the product drive it with `default-group` (the grouping column(s)). [element] obs-table: `group-by="<columnKey>"` renders a grey group-header band with a chevron + count; click to collapse/expand. Hide the grouping UI with `.hide-grouping` when needed.
grouping.dontUse: Don't use grouping to show nested record hierarchy — that's the `tree` variant. If the bands must NOT collapse (a static report where all child rows stay visible and there's no chevron) use the `pivot` variant (group-collapsible=false). For a flat sorted list, plain `basic` is enough.
grouping.example: Alert / event lists grouped by a column (e.g. by severity or source) with a count badge per group; [element] group-by="env" buckets monitors under Production / Staging.

cell-types.useWhen: Columns need rich, non-plain-text rendering. Each column renders through a named slot (`status`, `name`, `tags`, `severity`, `value`, `duration`, `action`, `monitorType`, `timestamp`, `count`, …), so a cell can be a status tag, a severity dot, tags, a sparkline, a color-coded threshold cell (`color-coded-cell.vue`, heatmap-style / `relative-percent` inline bar), or a row-actions kebab (`FlotoGridActions`).
cell-types.dontUse: Don't reach for custom cell slots when a column is plain sortable text — leave it as `basic`. Don't put a bulk multi-select checkbox here (that's `selectable`) or the row expander (that's `expandable`); those are dedicated props/columns, not cell slots.
cell-types.example: Monitor grid cells: a status tag (MStatusTag), a severity dot, tags, a value sparkline, and a trailing kebab cell (FlotoGridActions) for per-row actions.

pagination.useWhen: The dataset spans multiple pages. Use client paging (`paging` + `default-page-size`) for in-memory lists; use server paging (`external-take` / `external-skip` + `total-count` + `@data-state-change`) to fetch only the visible page for large/server-driven datasets. FlotoPaginatedCrud wires this up for fetched list pages.
pagination.dontUse: Don't client-load huge datasets — server-page them. Don't hand-roll paging controls; MGrid / FlotoPaginatedCrud own paging, sort, and filter. For live socket/widget-pushed feeds use the streaming grid (`api-socket-grid`, no paging) rather than paginating.
pagination.example: Large inventory / settings list pages server-paged through FlotoPaginatedCrud, fetching only the current page from the API.

tree.useWhen: Data is genuinely hierarchical — parent rows with nested child rows across levels. Use the `tabular-content-grid` tree (`expandable` with a `detailRow` of nested child rows, chevron + indentation per level).
tree.dontUse: Don't use `tree` for a single row's flat detail panel — plain `expandable` is enough. Don't use it for flat grouped buckets (`grouping`) or cross-tab metric summaries (`pivot`).
tree.example: SNMP OID / MIB trees — expand a parent OID to reveal indented child OID rows level by level.

pivot.useWhen: A static report/pivot grid: rows grouped under band headers that NEVER collapse — no chevron, no count, every child row always visible. [element] obs-table: `group-by="<key>"` + `group-collapsible="false"`. NOTE: this is a custom-element boolean attribute, so it must be the string "false" (group-collapsible="false") — omitting it leaves grouping collapsible (the default).
pivot.dontUse: Don't use `pivot` for ordinary grouped list rows that a user collapses/expands — that's `grouping` (the collapsible default). Don't use it for a single-record transposed key/value view — that's obs-key-value — or a big-value metric list — that's obs-metric-list.
pivot.example: A report widget grouping monitors by environment where every row must stay visible (no expand/collapse) — group-by="env" group-collapsible="false".

editable.useWhen: A user edits row values IN PLACE, without opening a separate form/drawer/modal — quick edits to a couple of fields. [element] obs-table: set `editable`, and mark each editable column with `editable:true`. A pencil appears per row; clicking it turns that row's editable columns into obs-inputs with Save / Cancel (obs-link). Listen to `save` ({id, values}) to persist, `canceledit` to discard.
editable.dontUse: Don't use inline editing for a full record with many fields, validation, or related sections — use a drawer or modal form (obs-drawer / obs-modal) instead. Don't make identity/computed/status columns editable (leave those as display cells).
editable.example: A monitor list where an operator quickly renames a monitor or fixes its IP/owner inline, then Save — without leaving the list.

styleVariants.useWhen: You need to tune the grid chrome for a context. [element] obs-table: `variant="bordered"` (internal column+row grid, no outer frame) for a dense data grid; `variant="borderless-rows"` (no row dividers, airy spacing) for a light widget list; `header-style="tinted"` for the item-list tinted header bar; `hide-header` for compact widget grids with no header row.
styleVariants.dontUse: Don't add an outer surrounding border — the product grid is borderless (bordered only draws the internal cell grid). Don't mix hide-header with sortable headers (there's no header to click).
styleVariants.example: A compact dashboard widget grid using borderless-rows + hide-header; a dense settings table using variant="bordered".

header-style.useWhen: header-style="default" (transparent header + bottom rule) for LIST/report screens — this is what the product uses. header-style="tinted" (grey band) only for a dense item-list table where the product uses the tinted header.
header-style.dontUse: tinted on a normal list/report grid — it paints a grey band the product does not have (both values pass conformance, so this wrong guess is invisible to automated checks).
header-style.must: default is the list-screen norm (it is also the element default — omit the attribute).
header-style.example: <obs-table columns=... rows=...></obs-table>  (default header — correct for list screens)

cell-content.useWhen: a column needs a real control/link, not text: type="switch" (boolean cell → obs-switch), type="icon" (clickable obs-icon; cell = icon name or {icon,label}), type="link" (cell = {text,href,icon?} or a string), type="button" (cell = {text?,icon?,variant?}). Activating any of them emits `cellaction` {id,key,type,value}.
cell-content.dontUse: passing raw <obs-*> markup as a cell VALUE — cell values are escaped as text. Use the typed cell instead.
cell-content.must: handle `cellaction` to react. For a two-control cell (the product NAME column: a ★ that favourites + text that opens), use type="link" with a leading icon and read `part` in the payload — `part:"icon"` (the icon was clicked) vs `part:"text"` (the label was clicked).

logo-cell.useWhen: a column shows a technology/vendor/monitor-TYPE and the product reference renders a COLOURED brand logo (not a monochrome UI glyph). The inventory Monitors table's TYPE column is the canonical case — Azure Cloud, Windows, Linux, MySQL, VMware ESXi… each a full-colour vendor mark. Set type="logo"; the cell value is a logo name string, an object {name,variant?,size?,title?}, or an ARRAY of those (rendered side by side, e.g. a base OS + a role mark). Default size ~18px, variant "color".
logo-cell.dontUse: Don't use type="icon" (monochrome glyph) for a real vendor/technology brand mark — the DS rule is icons default monochrome, but use COLOURED brand logos when the product reference shows them. Don't hand-draw an SVG; every mark comes from obs-logo. The full logo set requires the consumer to `import '@mtdt/observeops-ds-elements/logos'` — without it, only the built-in common set resolves and unknown names render the no-icon placeholder (obs-logo warns). Use variant:'line' only for a deliberately monochrome secondary mark.
logo-cell.must: for the inventory TYPE column, drive the cell with the monitor-type/vendor logo name (azure-cloud, windows, linux, mysql, vmware-esxi, …). A row that carries two marks (base + role) uses an array value.
logo-cell.example: columns:[{key:"type",title:"Type",type:"logo"}] with row.type="azure-cloud" (one coloured mark) or row.type=[{name:"linux"},{name:"docker"}] (two marks side by side)

sticky-header.useWhen: the header should stay visible while the body scrolls — set sticky-header AND max-height="<px>" for a self-contained scroll box.
sticky-header.dontUse: sticky-header without a bounded height (nothing scrolls) unless an ancestor is the scroll container.

do: Put row actions in a kebab cell; multi-select via the bulk bar
Keep the header visible in empty/loading states
[element] Give rows a stable `id`; drive rich cells via each column's `type`; persist inline edits from the `save` event
[element] Use group-collapsible="false" for a static report grid; `tree` (children) for real hierarchy
dont: Don't use a grid for a handful of static key/values (use obs-key-value) or big-value metrics (use obs-metric-list)
Don't hand-roll selection/paging — MGrid/FlotoPaginatedCrud own it
Don't inline-edit a whole record with validation — use a drawer/modal form; keep inline editing to a few quick fields
Don't add an outer surrounding border — the product grid is borderless (bordered = internal cell grid only)

F1.issue: Heavy: Kendo grid + 2 web workers (gridWorker/arrayWorker) — not trivially renderable outside the app (Storybook shows reproductions).

F2.issue: Kendo grid semantics — verify rows/cells expose proper table roles, sort state (aria-sort), and selection (aria-selected); the custom cell slots can lose them.

F3.issue: [element] obs-table is FUNCTIONAL: pass columns + rows (JSON/array); it sorts, selects (reflects el.selected), paginates, supports grouping (collapsible OR pivot/report via group-collapsible=false) + inline editing (editable), and emits change/sort/rowaction/pagechange/rowclick/edit/save/canceledit. It reproduces the product's Kendo <Grid> chrome (the live grid is store/worker/virtualised-bound) and COMPOSES the DS primitives — obs-checkbox (selection), obs-tag (status cells), obs-menu (row actions), obs-icon (glyphs) — rather than re-implementing them.

changelog: 2026-09-16 — (owner) Selection UX overhaul: DROPPED the old top-left "N items selected" pill (obs-tag). Instead, when rows are selected obs-table now shows the DS BULK ACTION BAR (obs-toolbar variant=bulk) FLOATING, centered, sticky just ABOVE the pager (the SaaS pattern) — it carries the selection count + a clear, and the consumer's action buttons come from the new `bulk-actions` slot (slot="bulk-actions" on each real element). obs-table composes obs-toolbar internally; the bar animates in. The `hide-selection-info` prop is now a no-op (deprecated — the old pill it hid is gone).

2026-09-16 — (owner-caught) FIX: after the obs-pagination extraction, changing page / page-size updated the footer's RANGE but did NOT re-slice the rows (the pager moved, the table didn't). Cause: defineCustomElement wraps emit() payloads as an ARRAY on the CustomEvent (e.detail = [value]), so obs-table's `onPagerPage`/`onPagerSize` handlers — which read e.detail expecting a plain number — hit their `typeof === 'number'` guard as false and no-op'd. Now they unwrap (`Array.isArray(e.detail) ? e.detail[0] : e.detail`). Verified: size 10 → page 1 renders 10 rows, page 2 renders the remaining 2.

2026-09-16 — (owner) The pagination footer now HIDES entirely when there are fewer rows than the smallest page size (min 10) — below that there's nothing to paginate, so the pager + legend disappear and reappear only at ≥10 rows (showPager = paged && rows >= min(size,10)). Also: the Monitors-style severity legend in the footer slot should be the DS `obs-severity-legend` (composes obs-severity, collapses to a '+N' pile with a hover popover when narrow) — see the severity-legend registry — not hand-rolled dots.

2026-09-15 — (owner) The pagination footer is now the standalone `obs-pagination` DS element (extracted so card/list views can reuse it — the product reuses its Kendo pager the same way). obs-table COMPOSES it: passes total/page/page-size, applies its pagechange/sizechange to the row-slice state, and forwards its own `footer` slot into obs-pagination's center slot. Pixel-identical footer; NO obs-table API change (same `pagechange` event, same `footer` slot, same SPLIT/CENTERED variants). See the `pagination` registry.

2026-09-15 — (owner) TWO pagination-footer variants via a new `footer` SLOT. The footer is now a 3-zone flex row: pager (left) · centered `footer` slot · item total (right). Leave the slot empty → SPLIT variant (pager left, total right — the existing default, unchanged). Fill it (e.g. a severity legend) → CENTERED variant (pager left, legend centered, total right — the product Monitors list page). One layout, both variants; the center zone is flex:1 so it collapses to a spacer when empty. Note: pagination still lives INSIDE obs-table (not a standalone obs-pagination) — extraction is a possible future step since the product reuses the Kendo pager in its card view.

2026-09-15 — (owner) Page-size select dropdown arrow fixed. The native <select> arrow sat flush against the right edge with a wide default text→arrow gap. Removed it (appearance:none) and overlaid an obs-icon chevronDown positioned by us (absolute, right:8px) — real whitespace before the right edge and a tight text→arrow gap. Select wrapped in a .psize-wrap; padding 0 24px 0 8px leaves room for the caret.

2026-09-15 — (owner) The page-size select (.psize) now matches the page-number squares: 28px height + 4px border-radius (was padding-driven height + 2px radius), so the whole pager row lines up at one consistent height.

2026-09-15 — (owner) Pager cells are now uniform SQUARES matching the product (equal boxes for page numbers AND nav icons). Was `min-width:22px` + `padding:2px 6px` (rectangles + uneven wide gaps); now every .ppage is a 28x28 centered flex box (min-width so a 3-digit page can still grow), border-radius 4px. Fixes both the rectangular shape and the too-large spacing between the left/right icon pairs.

2026-09-15 — (owner) Pager arrows are now Google MATERIAL SYMBOLS skip glyphs (owner supplied the shadcn.io/Iconify skip-previous + skip-next icons). Added 4 DS-local obs-icons (build-icons.mjs EXTRA): `skipPrevious` (|◀) + `skipNext` (▶|) with the stopper bar for first/last, and `skipPreviousNoLine` (◀) + `skipNextNoLine` (▶) — the same glyph with the bar subpath removed — for prev/next. Wired the pager to them (first=skipPrevious, prev=skipPreviousNoLine, next=skipNextNoLine, last=skipNext). Supersedes the earlier chevrons → outline play+CSS-bar → FA-solid caret/step iterations. All real obs-icons (passes the icon-reuse gate). Active page keeps --pagination-active-bg; numbered links + size select unchanged. Icon set now 643.

2026-09-15 — (owner) Two tweaks: (1) default header row is a touch taller — hs-default th padding 4px → 6px vertical, so the header is 31px (was 27px); data rows stay 41px. (2) A SELECTED row no longer gets a background FILL — removed `tr.row-selected td { background: --neutral-lightest }`. Selection now reads from the checked box + the thin --primary LEFT ACCENT bar only (`tr.row-selected td:first-child` inset box-shadow), which is retained; the hover tint is unchanged. Lighter, less heavy-handed selected state.

2026-09-15 — Fix (owner-caught): the sticky header's TOP + BOTTOM rules are now INSET box-shadows on `thead th` (`inset 0 1px 0` top, `inset 0 -1px 0` bottom), replacing the per-th `border-bottom`. Why: a `border-bottom` on a `position:sticky` <th> is clipped/scrolled away as rows slide under the pinned header (divider vanished on scroll); an OUTSET bottom shadow fixed the scrolled case but was occluded by the first data row AT REST (divider vanished at rest). INSET shadows paint inside the cell's own border-box — always rendered, never clipped by overflow or occluded by a sibling row — so the header divider is a single crisp line in BOTH states. Removed the redundant `border-bottom` from hs-default and hs-tinted.

2026-09-15 — DEFAULT sticky header + pinned pager + auto horizontal scroll (owner). The table is now a flex COLUMN that fills its container's height: the header (<thead th> position:sticky, top:0, opaque --page-background-color background) always stays pinned at the top and the pager lives OUTSIDE the scroll region (.box) so it is always pinned at the bottom — the rows scroll between them. This auto-engages ONLY when the rows overflow the available height (a short container / lots of rows) and auto-disengages when they fit; no prop needed (the older `sticky-header`/`max-height` props still force it for a standalone table). Horizontal scroll is likewise automatic: the grid gets a computed min-width (Σ each column's minWidth|fixed-px width, else 132px, + 44px per checkbox/expander + 48px for a row-actions column), so when there are more columns than fit the viewport the .box scrolls horizontally, and it re-evaluates on viewport resize (columns hiding off-screen → scrollbar appears). Both behaviours are DEFAULT in the component. Requires the host to give the table a bounded height (flex:1; min-height:0 in a column layout) for the vertical case. Verified via Playwright: 520px-tall viewport → header stays on scroll + pager pinned below the scroll box; 760px-wide viewport → horizontal scroll engages. 0 console errors.

2026-09-15 — Sort on EVERY column + header hover affordance + one-line cell truncation + 1px checkbox border (owner). (1) All columns are now sortable by default — clicking any header sorts by it (opt out per-column with `sortable:false`); the sort arrow shows on the active column. (2) Header cells get a hover background (--grid-header-hover-bg → --neutral-lightest #ecf1f9) and a pointer cursor to signal they are clickable. (3) Data cells truncate to ONE line on the column width — severity-name and text cells are `.cell-clip` (display:block; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap) and the grid is `table-layout:fixed` so columns respect their widths and overflow ellipsises (was wrapping to 2 lines). (4) obs-checkbox border thinned 1.5px → 1px to match the product. No new tokens; no hardcoded colours.

2026-09-15 — Row dividers softened to --neutral-lightest (lighter than the header rules which stay --border-color), matching the product. Checkbox size reverted to the leaf default (no scale) — obs-checkbox now uses a softer 4px corner radius (var --checkbox-radius). full-width corrected to a full-BLEED (negative-margin via --table-bleed, default 20px) that keeps cell padding — it no longer strips the first/last cell padding.

2026-09-15 — Product-match polish (owner): (1) header labels now TRUNCATE with an ellipsis on overflow — each <th> label is overflow:hidden / text-overflow:ellipsis / nowrap with a `title` tooltip carrying the full label (narrow/many-column tables show "CURRENT VE…" like the product instead of wrapping/overflowing); (2) the selection checkbox (select-all + per-row) is slightly LARGER with softer corners (scaled ~1.2 from the checkbox cell → ~22.8px / ~3.6px radius) and stays centered; (3) tighter LEFT inset before the checkbox (~10px) and before the leading DATA cell when NOT selectable (~12px) — a compact left gutter matching the product in both selectable and non-selectable cases; (4) visible per-row DIVIDERS plus a header TOP rule (a line ABOVE and BELOW the header); (5) new `full-width` boolean — FLUSH edge-to-edge (leading cell's left pad + trailing cell's right pad removed; rules/dividers/hover span the whole width) vs the default slight inset; (6) a PRIMARY column — the first data column (or any column with `primary:true`) renders the record NAME bolder (500 vs the row's 400) and gets a DOTTED UNDERLINE on row hover, working for BOTH a `text` and a `severity` first column (CSS-only, tr:hover .primary-cell .primary-text); (7) `selectable` documented as a first-class optional toggle (checkboxes present when set, absent otherwise; correct tight left inset in both cases). All via the DS --border-color token; no new tokens, no hardcoded colours.

2026-09-15 — New `logo` cell type + multi-glyph cells: a column type="logo" renders COLOURED brand/vendor marks via obs-logo (the product inventory Monitors TYPE column — Azure Cloud, Windows, Linux, MySQL, VMware ESXi…). The cell value is a logo name string, an object {name,variant?,size?,title?}, or an ARRAY of those rendered side by side (default variant="color", size ~18px; variant:"line" for a monochrome secondary mark). Also added multi-glyph support to the existing `icon` cell type: an ARRAY cell value renders each name as an obs-icon side by side (single string/object behaviour — the clickable glyph that emits `cellaction` — is unchanged). The full logo set needs the consumer to `import '@mtdt/observeops-ds-elements/logos'`. Reinforces the DS rule: icons default monochrome, use coloured brand logos when the product reference shows them.

2026-08-09 — Cell content follow-up (gap G15): a `link` cell can now carry TWO independent controls — the leading icon vs the text. `cellaction` includes `part`:"icon"|"text" so a consumer distinguishes "favourite this" (icon) from "open this" (text), exactly like the product NAME column. The icon click no longer navigates the link. Removes the shadow-root workaround.

2026-08-07 — Tier 3 (gaps G1 + G13a): added interactive CELL CONTENT — column type="switch"|"icon"|"link"|"button" render real DS elements (obs-switch/obs-icon/obs-link-style anchor/obs-button) and emit a `cellaction` {id,key,type,value} event (previously cell values were escaped as text, blocking 4 columns of the product Report grid). Added a STICKY HEADER: `sticky-header` + `max-height` pin the header while the body scrolls (no more injecting position:sticky into the shadow root).

2026-08-07 — Docs (gap G13b): stated that list/report screens use header-style="default" (the element default); "tinted" is only for the dense item-list variant. A wrong guess here is invisible to conformance (both are valid styles).

changelog.change: Fixed: sortable is now [Boolean,String] so sortable="false" actually disables column sorting (a pure Boolean coerced the string to true). Playground toggle can now turn sorting off.

changelog: 2026-07-14: pager first-page arrow fixed (owner) — the « (first) button used chevronDoubleRight + a scaleX(-1) class, which doesn't reliably flip on obs-icon; switched to the real chevronDoubleLeft icon so it renders « correctly.

2026-07-13: severity cells compose <obs-severity> + tighter checkbox column (owner) — the `severity` and `dot` cell types were hand-drawing their own ring/dot spans; they now render the DS <obs-severity> indicator (shape=dot; `dot` cells use display-text for the level label). Also tightened the selection checkbox column (was a double-16px gap: checkbox-cell pad-right + first-column pad-left) so the checkbox sits close to the first column. Both flow into obs-grid-select (which composes obs-table).

2026-07-13: dark-mode tinted header fix (owner) — header-style="tinted" text used --neutral-dark, which resolves near-black (#172336) in dark mode → invisible on the dark tinted bar. Switched to --text-color-common-primery (the same token the default header uses; flips to white-80% in dark). Readable in both themes.

2026-07-13: inline-edit column left-aligned (owner) — the edit column (pencil + Save/Cancel) was centered, so the pencil and the Save/Cancel links sat at different x positions row-to-row; changed .edit-col to text-align:left so they line up on a consistent left edge.

2026-07-13: inline-edit Save/Cancel now use obs-link (owner) — the inline-edit actions were plain anchors; swapped to the DS <obs-link> so they get the standard dotted-underline link treatment (obs-link owns colour + underline). Reuses the DS link primitive instead of ad-hoc anchors.

2026-07-13: pivot/report + inline-editing (owner) — the two previously-deferred variants are now real element features. (1) `group-collapsible="false"` turns grouping into a pivot/report grid: no chevron, no count, every child row always visible (a static report layout). (2) `editable` adds inline editing — a pencil per row; while a row is edited each column marked `editable:true` becomes an obs-input, with Save/Cancel; emits `edit`/`save` {id,values}/`canceledit`. Both showcased in the Elements gallery.

2026-07-13: variant completeness (owner) — added the remaining table-native Storybook variants: `heat` + `bar` cell types (color-coded threshold cells via column colorKey, and inline relative-percent bars) and the `tree` variant (hierarchical rows via `children`, chevron + indent, default-expanded). vertical-value + key-value were split into their OWN components (obs-metric-list, obs-key-value) since they are metric/detail LAYOUTS, not data tables. Pivot + inline-editing were the last deferred items (now shipped, see the later entry).

2026-07-13: vertical-align — REAL fix (owner re-caught). td vertical-align:middle alone left checkbox/actions/tag a few px high because the composed hosts (obs-tag/obs-checkbox/obs-menu) render display:inline → their host box is line-height-sized (15px) while the visible content is 19-22px, so it overflows and centering is thrown off. Forced those hosts to display:inline-flex in table cells → the host sizes to its content and vertical-align:middle now centers the VISIBLE box. Every cell type now measures gapTop===gapBottom.

2026-07-13: style-variant tweaks (owner) — `bordered` now shows only the INTERNAL cell grid (column + row dividers), with the outer left/right frame removed; `divided` (column rules) was replaced by `borderless-rows` — no row dividers (just the header underline) with airy row spacing.

2026-07-13: cell-types completeness (owner) — added the missing rich cell types from the Storybook Cell-types story: `dot` (a filled --severity-<value> dot + label, distinct from the hollow `severity` ring) and `sparkline` (an inline trend line from a numeric array). The Cell-types gallery now shows name · status · severity dot · tags · sparkline · actions, matching the product per-column slots.

2026-07-13: vertical-align fix (owner) — cell content was top-aligned (td default vertical-align:baseline) when a row was taller than a cell; added vertical-align:middle on th/td so EVERY cell type (checkbox · severity · type icons · status tag · text · actions) centers vertically, across all variants.

2026-07-13: grouping divider (owner) — adjacent collapsed group-header rows merged (same grey + the --border-color rule is invisible against it); added a 2px --page-background-color separator between group bands so they read as distinct sections. Keeps the neutral grey.

2026-07-13: expandable + grouping polish (owner) — the expandable detail row now fills the ENTIRE row width (not just from the first column) with a LIGHTER tint (--neutral-lightest #ecf1f9, was the darker #e3e8f2), content still aligned to the first data column; the grouping group-header rows now use a NEUTRAL GREY (--neutral-lighter #e3e8f2) instead of the light blue, so they read as a section divider distinct from the blue row-selection.

2026-07-13: expandable detail-row fix (owner-caught) — the detail now matches the product .ds-grid-detail: a --table-details-bg framed box that starts at the FIRST DATA column (empty leading cells for the chevron/checkbox columns), left-aligned under the parent's first column content — not a full-width fill from the left edge.

2026-07-13: variant coverage — added the Storybook table variants as real element features: expandable (chevron column + detail rows), group-by (collapsible group-header rows with counts), header-style tinted (item-list bar), variant (bordered / divided / borderless), hide-header, disabled selection (row `disabled` → disabled checkbox), and a `tags` cell type (obs-tag chips). Showcased all in the Elements gallery; the playground is now full-width. Advanced Kendo-only variants (tree, pivot, inline-editing, key-value / vertical-value, color-coded heatmap cells) remain Storybook reproductions, not yet in the obs-table element.

2026-07-13: fidelity fix #5 (owner-caught) — (1) reverted the pager first/last to the real library icons (chevronDoubleRight, flipped « for first) instead of the hand-composed seekFirst/seekLast (removed from _icons.js — no hand-drawn glyphs); (2) tightened the header row (padding 6px→4px, now ~28px vs ~41px data rows) so the header — including the select-all checkbox — reads crisp/compact like the product, not spacious.

2026-07-13: fidelity fix #4 (owner-caught) — pager first/last arrows now match the product Kendo .k-grid-pager: |◀ (seekFirst) and ▶| (seekLast) — a chevron + bar — instead of the double-chevrons (« ») used before. Added seekFirst/seekLast to the icon library (the Kendo pager glyphs, not in the FA icons.js), rendered via obs-icon.

2026-07-13: fidelity fix #2 (owner-caught) — sort indicator, pager, and border corrected: the sorted column now turns --primary and shows a straight long-arrow-up/down (obs-icon longArrowUp/longArrowDown; the first pass used a chevron with no colour change), the pager first/last arrows render correctly (« … ») with the page-size 'items per page' select added, and one border now encloses the table + pager as a single .box. 2026-07-13: shipped the real <obs-table> web component — the DS data table (Kendo Grid / VirtualTable chrome). Columns + rows, sortable headers, checkbox selection + select-all (reflects el.selected), rich cells (severity ring / status tag / type icons), a per-row actions menu, pagination, empty + loading states.
